summary: A listed company must handle its share transfer work either on its own or through an outside expert registered with the Board. If the company handles it alone and the security holders cross one lakh, it must hire a registered expert or register itself. Any change in this expert requires a special three-way agreement and notice to the stock exchange.
points: The listed entity must appoint a registrar to an issue and share transfer agent or manage the facility in-house.
If in-house holders exceed one lakh, the entity must register with the Board or appoint a registered agent.
The entity must ensure all share transfer activities are maintained in-house or by a registered agent.
When changing or appointing a new agent, the entity must sign a tripartite agreement or an agreement with the new agent.
The entity must inform the stock exchange about the appointment within seven days of the agreement.
The agreement must be placed in the subsequent meeting of the board of directors.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited managed its own share transfers for its investors. Over time, the total number of security holders crossed one lakh. To follow the rules, Meera Textiles decided to appoint an outside expert. It chose Alpha Share Services Private Limited, which was registered with the Board. Meera Textiles signed a proper agreement with Alpha Share Services, informed the stock exchange within seven days, and placed the agreement before its board of directors in their very next meeting.

terms.term: Registrar to an issue and share transfer agent
terms.meaning: An expert helper who manages share records and transfers for a company.
Done by the company itself instead of hiring an outside helper.
A legal contract signed by three different parties.

watch: Mutual funds issuing listed units do not have to follow the requirements of this regulation.
